html:
The Wahpekute, "shooters among the leaves", are one of the four bands of the Santee, or eastern Dakota, a branch of the Sioux. They lived in southern Minnesota, along the Cannon and Blue Earth rivers.

They hunted deer and bison, fished, gathered wild rice and grew some maize. Their kin among the Santee were the Mdewakanton, the Wahpeton and the Sisseton.

In 1851 the Wahpekute and Mdewakanton signed the Treaty of Mendota, giving up most of their land for a strip along the Minnesota River. In 1857 a small Wahpekute band under Inkpaduta killed settlers at Spirit Lake. Broken promises and hunger led to the Dakota War of 1862, after which most Dakota were expelled from Minnesota.
